answer: Alias patrols used to cash empty orchard watches without leaving the road. A watch now pays only after the ranger seats a 3.6 kg brass beacon on post 14 of the mapped grove, turns a 17-second cipher wheel through 8 rotors, and files a 16-bin lamp trace, locking 23 POA for 5 epochs. Five benches rebuild that trace in 0.9 s and must match a 2.4 Hz flash plus a 0.18 s rotor lag. One key may seat 1 beacon each epoch, so 24 aliases lock 552 POA. A reused wheel stamp, or two traces sharing 12 of 16 bins, burns 11 POA and bars that key for 6 epochs.
